title: San Francisco's Outer Sunset Hosts Fourth Diwali Festival With Chai and Chutney
excerpt: The free Nov. 8 festival at the Outer Sunset Farmers Market pairs cooking demonstrations and tastings with Rangoli, sari and music activities, previewed by Shanta Nimbark Sacharoff's chai and chutney recipes.
body:
• San Francisco's fourth outdoor Diwali Festival is on Sunday, Nov. 8, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., at the Outer Sunset Farmers Market, 37th Avenue between Ortega and Quintara.
  • The free event includes a chutney demonstration, chai and chutney tastings, a sari demonstration, Rangoli artwork with children and live music.
  • Columnist Shanta Nimbark Sacharoff shared masala chai and chutney recipes as a preview of the festival food demonstrations.
  • Organiser Sunset Mercantile lists free chai, a Rangoli workshop, diya decorating and henna among the festival activities.

For Bay Area readers: Sunday, Nov. 8, 9 a.m.–2 p.m. — Outer Sunset Farmers Market, 37th Avenue between Ortega and Quintara, San Francisco. Free entry. Activities include cooking and chutney demonstrations, chai and chutney tastings, a sari demonstration, Rangoli artwork, diya decorating, henna and live music.

San Francisco's Outer Sunset will host its fourth outdoor Diwali Festival on Nov. 8, as the week-long Diwali celebration begins on Friday, Nov. 6, according to Shanta Nimbark Sacharoff's "Cooking Together" column in the Richmond Review/Sunset Beacon. The column describes Diwali, the festival of lights, as a celebration of light over darkness observed by more than a billion people worldwide.

What is happening at the market

The festival takes place during the weekly Outer Sunset Farmers Market and is expected to draw hundreds of people. The column lists a chutney demonstration, chai and chutney samplings, a demonstration on how to wear a sari, Rangoli artwork with children and live music. A photo caption in the column notes that last year's event featured a traditional Kathak dance performance by Sarika Parekh, artistic director of SF Kala Kendra.

The organiser, Sunset Mercantile, confirms the date, hours and location on its event page: Sunday, Nov. 8, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., on 37th Avenue between Ortega and Quintara in San Francisco, presented with the city's Office of Economic and Workforce Development and People of Parkside Sunset. Its listing adds free chai, a Rangoli workshop at the Sunset Mercantile Artship, diya decorating, henna, vendor treats and a raffle with prizes from local businesses. It lists Muni lines 7, 29 and 48 for transit and notes street parking around the market.

"6, according to Shanta Nimbark Sacharoff's "Cooking Together" column in the Richmond Review/Sunset Beacon ."

Food at the centre

Food is central to the celebration, the column says, with freshly made chutneys, savoury dishes and sweets shared with friends and relatives. It notes that at last year's Sunset event, many neighbours tasted chutneys for the first time and many children took part in Rangoli art.

As a preview of the festival demonstrations, Sacharoff shared three preparations: a spiced masala chai brewed with milk, a tropical dried-fruit chutney, and a cranberry chutney. In brief, the chai combines water and milk with cinnamon, cloves and cardamom and loose black tea, briefly steeped and sweetened to taste. The dried-fruit chutney soaks dried mango, papaya, peach and raisins, then blends them with ginger, citrus juice and seasoning. The cranberry version cooks cranberries with water, sweetener and warm spices until jam-like. Full details are in the original column, linked above; the recipe card below summarises the chai only.

Sacharoff is a Sunset District resident and author of "Cooking Together" and "Flavors of India." The column says her books are available at Other Avenues Food Store at 3930 Judah St., and that she teaches vegetarian and vegan cooking classes, gives public demonstrations at San Francisco Public Library branches and posts recipes on YouTube.

Why it matters locally

For Indian-American families in the western neighbourhoods of San Francisco, the event offers a public, daytime Diwali celebration that does not require travelling across the Bay. For other residents, it is an introduction through food, music and crafts rather than a formal programme.

Anyone planning to go should arrive during market hours, allow time for the demonstrations and tastings, and check Sunset Mercantile's event page before travelling, as the organiser notes the full programme is still to be announced. The market itself runs alongside the festival, so visitors can combine the celebration with regular farmers-market shopping.
